facts.claim: A 2026 Nature Neuroscience study deliberately induced NREM-like cortical ON/OFF periods in awake sleep-deprived mice using optogenetic/genetic methods.

sources.title: Researchers trigger sleep’s restorative effect in parts of the awake brain
Induction of cortical ON/OFF periods in awake mice fulfills sleep functions

facts.notes: Keep species and intervention explicit. Do not generalize the induced effect directly to humans.

facts.claim: In that mouse study, stimulated regions later showed lower slow-wave activity during natural sleep, consistent with reduced local sleep need.

sources.title: Researchers trigger sleep’s restorative effect in parts of the awake brain

facts.notes: Phrase as local sleep need, not proof that total organism sleep need disappeared.

facts.claim: Sleep-deprived mice receiving the sleep-like stimulation in relevant sensory and motor regions performed similarly to well-rested mice on a tactile-memory task, while unstimulated sleep-deprived mice performed worse.

sources.title: Researchers trigger sleep’s restorative effect in parts of the awake brain

facts.notes: Describe the specific tactile-memory result only; do not imply broad cognition was fully restored.

facts.claim: Local slow-wave or sleep-like activity can appear during behavioral wakefulness, particularly after sleep deprivation.

sources.title: Researchers trigger sleep’s restorative effect in parts of the awake brain
Is Your Brain Sleeping While You're Awake?

facts.notes: Use local-sleep language rather than saying an awake person is globally asleep.

facts.claim: Whales and dolphins can use unihemispheric sleep, sleeping one cerebral hemisphere at a time while preserving swimming, breathing, and environmental awareness.

sources.title: Question of the Week: Dolphins and Whales on the High Seas
Behavioral, neurophysiological and evolutionary perspectives on unihemispheric sleep

facts.claim: Great frigatebirds have been directly recorded sleeping in flight, sometimes one hemisphere at a time and sometimes both; in the study they averaged about 0.69 hours of sleep per day while flying.

sources.title: Evidence that birds sleep in mid-flight

facts.notes: Do not imply the birds get normal land-like sleep totals while airborne.

facts.claim: A 2016 human first-night-effect study found hemispheric asymmetry in sleep depth in part of the default-mode network and stronger responsiveness to unusual sounds from the less-sleeping hemisphere during the first laboratory night.

sources.title: Night Watch in One Brain Hemisphere during Sleep Associated with the First-Night Effect in Humans

facts.notes: Do not equate this with full human unihemispheric sleep.

facts.claim: Later human work complicates the idea that hemispheric asymmetry alone explains the first-night effect, so the phenomenon should be presented as suggestive rather than a settled dolphin-like mechanism in humans.

sources.title: The first-night effect of sleep occurs over nonconsecutive nights in unfamiliar and familiar environments

facts.notes: This caveat is required in the human section.

facts.claim: The researchers behind the 2026 mouse study identified future investigation of non-invasive transcranial stimulation in humans as a research direction, but no human sleep-replacement effect has been demonstrated.

sources.title: Researchers trigger sleep’s restorative effect in parts of the awake brain

facts.notes: Future-facing only. Never turn this into a practical claim that people can skip sleep.
